sentences: I push the steel probe into the ground and note how far it travels before resistance stops it.
I collect a handful of topsoil from the garden bed and squeeze it to see if it holds together.
I mix a soil sample with distilled water and read the pH meter after it settles.
I dig a small pit and measure the depth of the dark surface layer with a ruler.
I check the moisture sensor reading at six inches and record the percentage in my log.
I turn over a spadeful of earth and count the earthworms visible in the clod.
I pour water into a hole and time how long it takes to drain away completely.
I rub a pinch of soil between my fingers to judge the proportion of sand and clay.
I spread a layer of compost over the bed and rake it into the top two inches.
I press a penetrometer into the soil and read the pressure gauge in pounds per square inch.
I sprinkle a sample with vinegar and watch for bubbles that indicate free carbonate.
I scoop soil from three spots in the field and combine them in a clean plastic bucket.
I set the oven to 105 degrees and dry the sample to constant weight.
I look at the color of the moist soil against a Munsell chart and write down the code.
I count the number of seeds that sprout in a tray of this soil after seven days.
I pour a soil slurry through a sieve and collect the fine particles in a beaker.
I push a trowel into the crusted surface and lift a slab to inspect the structure.
I scatter gypsum pellets across the plot and water them in to reduce the sodium level.
I walk the rows and note where water pools after a heavy rain, marking the low spots.
I cover the bare ground with straw and check that the layer stays three inches thick.
